# What a reply holds — documents, records, memory and names

**Shared across every skill.** Four rules about what goes in front of the
person and where things are kept.

---

## Documents are printed in full; records are summarised

A **document** is what a person reads, signs or sends: the quote, the cost
sheet, the NCR, the 8D, the RFQ package, an email draft, the morning report,
the intake form. **It is printed in the reply, in full.** Saving a copy to a
file as well is fine; a file *instead of* the reply is not. The person reads
the reply, and every delimited block and outbound check lives in it.

### Reports are the exception: a short reply when the page was written

The morning report, the Operations page and the supplier bid comparison are
read on a page, not in the chat. For
the bid comparison the headline is the provisional recommendation and its main
tradeoff, the exceptions are the requirements still open before an award, and
the decision waiting is the next-step question. **When this run wrote the full page
somewhere the person can open** (a publish returned its URL, or the page was
saved as an HTML file and the reply names the file), the reply is a summary
of about 150 words. **200 words is a hard limit: count before sending.** Each
item below is one sentence; an exception or a decision is the thing and its
number, with the explanation left on the page.

1. Safety first, one line per item: a safety-flagged record, a record under
   *"Blocked — safety status unknown"*, or *"Safety status: not assessed"*.
2. The site, the production day, and the freshness state in one line: data
   complete, or the gap.
3. The headline: good output against plan, and OEE or why it is not computed.
4. Up to three exceptions, one line each.
5. The decisions waiting today, or *"No decisions waiting today."*
6. Where the full page is: the URL or the file path.

No tables, logs or methods in the summary; they are on the page. Every
number in the summary is one the page prints. **This is for the whole
report only.** A request that picks sections or skips some ("freshness and
the rankings, skip OEE this time"), a question, a record the person asked to
see, or text to paste is answered in the reply in full, in report order, as
always; the page may still be saved as well. **When nothing could be written**
(no file writer and no publish), the page is printed in the reply in full, as
above. Where a skill offers "the page in the conversation", a saved file named
in the reply is that offer. Documents someone signs or sends (quotes, NCRs,
8Ds, RFQ packages, email drafts) are always printed in full.

### Saved copies: Word for documents, Excel for tables, never .txt

When a document is also saved as a file, and it should be wherever the person
downloads from a file card (Cowork), the file is one a plant opens without
thinking about it:

| What it is | File |
|---|---|
| A controlled document: customer quote, supplier RFQ package, NCR, escape notification, 8D, trade study memo | `.docx` |
| A table someone works in: internal cost sheet, bid comparison, ranked candidates, scrap or downtime lists | `.xlsx` |
| A report or dashboard | the HTML page, per `artifact-style.md` |
| A record (contract payload, day record, register row) | its contract's format, as below |

**Never `.txt` or `.md` for a document.** A plain-text quote reads as a draft
nobody finished, and it is what a person gets when no format is named.

- **How.** Use the session's Word or Excel skill where there is one (Cowork
  has both); else `python-docx` or `openpyxl` where already installed. Never
  install a package for it and never hand-build the file's XML: a file Word
  cannot open is worse than none. With no writer, write no file and say so in
  one line: *"No Word copy this session: no Word writer available."* The
  reply already holds the document.
- **The plant's template.** A controlled document keeps the structure
  `onboarding` captured. Where that example is a `.docx` in the documents
  folder, start the Word copy from that file; otherwise use a plain layout
  and keep the *template not on file* flag the document already carries.
- **What goes in which file.** The customer's file holds only what the
  sendable block holds. Internal figures (hours, rates, margin, the cost
  build-up) go in their own file, the internal cost sheet, and never into the
  customer's.
- **Names.** What it is and its reference: `quote-Q-EXAMPLE-MEDICAL-4402A-01.docx`,
  `cost-sheet-Q-EXAMPLE-MEDICAL-4402A-01.xlsx`, `NCR-2026-0141.docx`. Name each file in
  the reply.

A **record** is a handoff to another skill or a store: a contract payload (a
downtime record, a geometry estimate), a register row, a pulse day record, a
supplier bid record, a selection record, a sourcing-event row. **It is never
pasted into the reply as a raw YAML or JSON block.** A quality manager, a
buyer or an estimator should not have to read 150 lines of field names to
find out what happened.

Instead:

1. **Save the full record** where its contract says, or to a file next to the
   run's other outputs, and **name the file** in the reply.
2. **Show a short table of the fields a person decides on**, under their
   contract names so nothing is lost in translation — the key, the status,
   and whichever of these the record has: `fields_missing`, `data_complete`,
   `decided_by`, `decided_at`, `follows_recommendation`, `actuals_confidence`,
   `geometry_path`, `reading_basis`, `approval`. One row per record, or one
   row per field for a single record. Never more than about a dozen rows.
3. **If the record cannot be saved** (no write access this session), print it
   in full, **as a table, not a code block**, marked *not stored — paste this
   back next time*.

The person can always ask for the raw record ("show me the YAML"). Then print
it.

# Command-center pages — what they are, and what they are not

Every chain carries a `Command center:` line naming the page a run
feeds — Sales, Quality, Operations, Supply Chain. This file defines the shape
once, so five skills do not each invent one.

It exists because they were each inventing one, and inventing the same
contradiction: "updates open corrective actions," "updates the maintenance
panel," "attaches the NCR and the 8D." Read literally, those are writes into an
external system. The plugin's own binding rule says otherwise:

> **Microsoft 365 is read-only by default.** Write access is an admin opt-in and
> Teams has no write path at all. No skill may assume it can post a message or
> write a file back into M365.
> — `artifact-style.md`

Both statements cannot be true. This one wins, because it is the platform
constraint rather than a preference.

---

## What a command-center page actually is

**Two kinds, and a skill always knows which one it produced.**

**A live dashboard**, for Operations and Quality. Published to the user's
Claude artifact store on the first run and updated in place at the same URL on
every later run, per `live-dashboard.md`. The artifact store is the user's own
Claude account, not M365 and not a system of record, so publishing to it does
not break the rule above.

**An offered page**, for Sales and Supply Chain, and for Operations or Quality
whenever the dashboard could not be published this run. An artifact produced
in the conversation that the user places: a page they open, read, and save or
forward, written as **a replacement for the last one**, carrying the same
sections in the same order, so a person can put it where the previous version
lived and read the delta at a glance. The plugin does not put it there.

**"Updated" is allowed only after a successful publish.** A skill may say it
updated a dashboard only when the publish call returned a URL in this same
run. Everywhere else the page was *offered*, and the skill says so. Reporting a
panel as updated when a page was offered is the false statement this file was
written to stop, and it still is.

**The dashboard is private until the user shares it.** No skill shares it, and
no skill says it is shared.

## The four pages

| Page | Fed by | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| **Sales** | Chain 1, at quote release | Commercial performance for the period, with the intake record and the quote attached to the run |
| **Quality** | Chain 2, and Chain 5's quality half | Open corrective actions, with the NCR and the 8D by reference. **A live dashboard, the Quality Register**, written by `ncr-writeup` and `root-cause-capa` |
| **Operations** | Chain 3 nightly, Chain 4 on a breakdown | The morning numbers, the downtime log, exceptions, and the maintenance picture. **A live dashboard, published by Chain 3 only.** Chain 4, and `daily-production-report` run alone, offer the page in the conversation; two pages showing the same numbers is how a meeting ends up arguing about which is right |
| **Supply Chain** | Chain 5's sourcing half | The supplier signal and the sourcing package |

Chain 5 produces **two pages from one run** — Quality takes the corrective
action record, Supply Chain takes the supplier signal. They are separate
artifacts with separate audiences, not one page with two sections.

## The rules

**Say what actually happened.** *"Updated **Fairview: Operations Command
Center**, `<url>`. Private to you until you share it"* is honest when the
publish returned that URL in this run. *"Here is the Operations page for
8 September; save it over yesterday's"* is honest when it did not. *"Updated
the Operations command center"* with no URL behind it is not, and a plant
person who believes it will stop checking.

**Every command-center page ends with one of two lines**, not only the first
page in a run:

- **Published:** the dashboard line, with its name and URL.
- **Offered:** the placement line, *"save it over yesterday's"*, or where the
  last one lives. **A page that should have been a dashboard and was not also
  says so:** *"The dashboard was not updated: [reason]."* That fallback never
  stalls the run, and never offers to publish later.

Chain 5 produces two pages; both end that way.

**When asked to do something the plugin never does, hand over the content and
say who acts.** Post to a channel, send the mail, close the ticket, update the
record: give the ready-to-use text, and say plainly that the user performs the
action. *"I don't post to Teams. Here's the text to paste."* **Never offer to
do it "once X is confirmed"** — *"confirm the channel and I will post exactly
this"* promises a capability that does not exist, and the person waits for a
post that never comes. Where the right content is a draft — a close-out note,
a channel message — produce it, labelled as a draft, rather than only saying
it cannot be filed.

**Say what was actually checked, by the call that checked it.** *"I searched
the public MCP registry"* when that is the call that ran. Not *"I checked your
connector directory"* and not *"three connectors are installed on this
account"* unless the account's own listing was queried in this run. A search of
one place reported as a check of another is a false statement about the user's
own systems, and it is the kind they act on.

**Attachments are references, not uploads.** "Attaches the NCR" means the page
carries the NCR's identifier and enough of it to be useful, so a reader can find
the full record. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.

**Sensitive values follow the audience rule.** A Sales page shown to a customer
carries no margin line; the internal one may. See `secret-config.md`.

**Absent is not zero.** A section with no data says so — *"no open corrective
actions in this window"* is different from an empty heading, and different again
from *"we could not read the quality library."* See `absent-is-not-zero.md`.

**House style applies.** Pages render per `artifact-style.md`, except a
con...[truncated]

# Artifact style — the house look

**Shared across the plugin.** One visual system so every page a skill produces
reads as the same product. Read this before building any HTML artifact; do not
invent a new palette per skill.

**The point is not decoration.** These are operating tools for a plant — a data
quality report, a morning production report, a bad-actor ranking, a cost-basis
sheet. Legible and defensible beats flashy. No hero banners, no marketing
gradients. A shop drawing, not a landing page.

---

## The constraint that shapes everything

**Microsoft 365 is read-only by default.** Write access is an admin opt-in and
Teams has no write path at all. No skill may assume it can post a message or
write a file back into M365.

So every deliverable is produced **in the conversation** and the user places it
themselves. An artifact is a thing they open, read, and save or forward. It is
never something the plugin filed away on their behalf.

**The one exception is the two live dashboards**, Operations and the Quality
Register, which are published to the user's own Claude artifact store and
updated in place, per `live-dashboard.md`. That store is not M365 and not a
system of record. Everything on this page applies to them unchanged.

---

## When to use an artifact, and when not to

Reach for a page when the output is something the user will **refer back to,
print, take into a meeting, or hand to someone else**. A data quality report, a
morning production report, a ranked diagnosis, a scored comparison. Skip it for
a single number or a one-line answer; the chat reply is the deliverable and a
page wrapped around one sentence is noise.

**The artifact is additive, never a replacement.** The user still gets the short
answer in chat. The page is where they go for the full picture.

**Three kinds of output, and only one of them is an artifact:**

| Output | Form | Why |
|---|---|---|
| A report, dashboard, or ranked analysis | HTML artifact, this style | Read at a glance, referred back to |
| A dataset | XLSX workbook, tab per entity | Meant to be filtered, pivoted, and checked |
| A controlled document | The plant's own template | An NCR, an 8D, a quote, a supplier RFQ package and a trade study memo all have a plant-specific or customer-specific shape, captured during `onboarding`. Never restyle a controlled document into the house look. |

That last row matters. A quality manager's 8D goes to a customer against a
contractual format. House styling it would be wrong, not nicer.

---

## Design tokens

Every color and font is a CSS custom property. Components never carry a literal
hex, so one override point recolors the whole page correctly.

```css
:root {
  --ink: #1A1D21;          /* primary text, graphite */
  --paper: #F2F3F5;        /* page background, cool grey */
  --paper-raised: #FFFFFF; /* card surfaces sitting on --paper */
  --line: #D6D9DD;         /* hairline borders and rules */
  --accent: #1F5C8B;       /* primary accent, drawing blue */
  --accent-soft: #E4EDF4;  /* accent tint for pills and highlights */

  /* Semantic, never repurposed as branding */
  --good: #2E7248;
  --good-soft: #E3EFE7;
  --warn: #A8641A;
  --warn-soft: #F7EBDA;
  --critical: #A93226;
  --critical-soft: #F9E9E7;

  --font-display: 'IBM Plex Sans Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif;
  --font-body: 'IBM Plex Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, sans-serif;
  --font-mono: 'IBM Plex Mono', 'SF Mono', Consolas, monospace;

# The hours step and the ladder

**Every machine hour on the internal sheet says where it came from.** An
estimator handed "op 20: 9.5 min/pc" cannot tell a number read off a current
routing from one Fusion produced with library feeds, and those two numbers
deserve very different amounts of trust. So each operation carries its rung,
its path, its cutting-data basis, its setup and run separately, a range, and
the variance against every other source that exists.

None of it reaches the customer. The customer quote carries prices; this file
is the internal sheet's business.

---

## What the hours step reads

| Input | From | When it is absent |
|---|---|---|
| Routings | `routings` tab, consolidated dataset v4, or a routing file | No rung 1. Say so per part |
| Operation actuals | `operation_actuals` tab, dataset v4, or an actuals file | No rung 2. Say so per part |
| Geometry estimate | `../../../shared/contracts/geometry-estimate.md`, from `rfq-to-quote` step 7 or typed by the estimator | No rung 3. The internal sheet says the design step did not run and why |
| Machine classes | `Machine classes` table under `### Machining data` in the `## Plant context` block: Machine class, Work centers, Cell, Setup hours, Tool change min, Basis | Setup at rung 3 cannot be taken from the plant. Name it; the estimator supplies it or the op falls to rung 4 |
| Cutting data | `Cutting data` table in the same section (Material, Tool class, SFM, Chip load ipt, Basis), or a line `Fusion tool library: <name>` | The CAM path runs on library feeds and every op is `fusion_default`, rung 4. The feature path cannot compute a cut time |
| Variance flag threshold | `Variance flag threshold: <percent>` in the same section | Use 15%, and print it as **"15% — default threshold, not plant-set"** wherever a flag depends on it |

A value tagged `Basis: assumed` in either table is used and labelled assumed on
every op it touches. It is the plant's number, recorded as a guess.

---

## The ladder, per operation

Best available first. **The highest rung that exists for an operation is its
basis; every other rung that exists is shown beside it as a cross-check.**

| Rung | What qualifies | What does not |

> Storage — the encrypted/secret side of config, not a plain-text config file

This file is what that rule actually means in a running plugin, so no skill
